title: Purification of differentiated tumor cells from medulloblastoma for transplantation into mouse cerebellum
protocol: Dissolve 100 U papain in 10 mL DPBS.
Add 200 μL DNase I to the papain solution and mix by inversion.
Add 2 mg L-cysteine into the papain-DNase I mixture.
Adjust pH of the papain solution until it becomes orange (pH 7.0–7.3) using 4-6 μL 2N NaOH.
Filter the papain solution with a 0.45 μm membrane to obtain the final papain solution.
Mix 200 μL DNase I in 5 mL DPBS and mix by inversion.
Add 1 mL Ovo stock solution into the DNase I-DPBS mixture to prepare the ovo solution.
Mix 38 mL neurobasal medium, 800 μL B27 supplement, 400 μL penicillin/streptomycin, 400 μL L-glutamine and 400 μL sodium pyruvate to prepare NB-B27 culture medium.
Adjust pH of the NB-B27 medium to 7.2–7.4 with 2N NaOH (4-6 μL).
Remove the mouse head with a cut posterior from the ears using surgical scissors.
Make a midline incision in the skin using the scissors.
Flip the skin over the eyes.
Hold the head with forceps.
Insert microdissection scissors into the foramen magnum and cut straight towards the eyes to access the brain.
Peel away the skull using forceps.
Pinch off the cerebellum using forceps.
Remove the brain stem (anterior to the cerebellum) as much as possible using forceps.
Cut cerebellar tissue into small (2–3 mm) pieces on a 6 cm plastic dish with 1–2 mL ice cold PBS, using a replacement blade.
Transfer tissue pieces to a 15 mL conical tube containing 10 mL Papain solution with DNase I and L-cysteine using a disposable plastic pipette.
Incubate the tissue at 37°C in a water bath for 30 min.
Aspirate off the papain solution.
Add 2 mL Ovo solution to the tissue pieces.
Gently triturate the tissue pieces using a Pasteur glass pipette (fire polished) with a bulb.
Let the tissue pieces settle for 1 min at 20°C–25°C, and transfer the top 1 mL suspension to a cell collection tube.
Add another 1 mL Ovo solution, and triturate again using a Pasteur pipet with a bulb.
Let the tissue pieces settle for 1 min, and transfer the top 1 mL suspension to the cell collection tube.
Add another 1 mL Ovo solution, and triturate using a P1000 pipette set to 1 mL with a sterilized pipette tip.
Pipette up and down 5 times.
Let the tissue pieces settle for 1 min, and transfer the top 1 mL suspension to the cell collection tube.
Repeat steps for another two times, and remove top 1.5 mL suspension to the cell collection tube.
Transfer all remaining solution/cells to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Triturate with a P200 pipette set to 200 μL with a sterilized pipette tip.
Pipette up and down 5 times.
Let the tissue pieces settle for 1 min, and transfer top solution (approximately 300 μL) into the cell collection tube.
Discard the remaining solution (~200 μL) at the bottom of the tube, which contains tissue debris.
Centrifuge cells at 220 × g in the cell collection tube for 10 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 6 mL DPBS-BSA.
Strain cells through a cell strainer (40 μm) into a 50 mL tube.
Remove tissue chunks that are not thoroughly dissociated by the trituration process.
Suck off liquid from underneath the strainer to minimize cell loss.
Transfer cell suspension from the 50 mL tube to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 220 × g and 4°C.
Remove supernatant after centrifugation.
Wash cells with 2-3 mL of PBS.
Repeat steps of centrifuging and washing the cells twice more.
Resuspend cell pellet in 5 mL NB-B27 after final wash.
Take 10 μL of cell suspension into an Eppendorf tube.
Add 190 μL of 0.4% Trypan Blue to the Eppendorf tube.
Mix gently and count live (unstained) cells using a hemocytometer.
Count dead cells stained with Trypan Blue separately for viability measurement.
Take the average count of live cells from each set of 16 corner squares.
Multiply by 104 to get the concentration of Trypan Blue-treated cell suspension.
Further multiply by 20 to correct for the 1:20 dilution due to Trypan Blue addition.
Calculate the total number of viable cells/mL in the original cell suspension (5 mL NB-B-27).
Add together the live and dead cell counts from each set of 16 corner squares to obtain a total cell count.
Divide the live cell count by the total cell count to calculate the percentage viability.
If over 5% of cells are dead, wash the cell suspension with NB-B27 medium by centrifugation at 220 × g for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 220 × g for 5 minutes and resuspend the cell pellet in FACS buffer.
Ensure all steps for cell immunolabelling are performed on ice.
Operate all centrifugations at 4°C.
Incubate the cells with the primary antibody against Tag1 in FACS buffer for 30 min.
Wash the cells with 2 mL PBS, centrifuge at 220 × g for 5 min and remove the supernatant.
Repeat washing step three times.
Incubate the cells with Alexa Fluor 594 goat anti-mouse IgM antibody in FACS buffer for 30 min in the dark.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of FACS buffer and centrifuge at 220 × g for 5 min.
Repeat washing step three times.
Add 5 μL of Propidium Iodide (PI) staining solution per 100 μL of cell suspension.
Incubate for 15 min on ice in the dark.
Exclude dead cells from the cell suspension on a BD FACS ARIA-II cytometer.
Harvest Tag1+ cells and Tag1- cells by FACS.
Purified cells are collected into 2–3 mL cold NB-B27 medium.
Keep purified cells on ice (up to 4 h) for transplantation into mouse cerebella.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 220 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the cell pellet in NB-B27 medium.
Quantify the number of live cells using a hemocytometer as described in steps 27–32.
Dilute the cell suspension to a density of 4–6 × 10^4 cells/μL in NB-B27 medium.
Keep the diluted cell suspension on ice until use.
Weigh mice using an animal weighing scale.
Administer Ketamine/Xylazine solution via intraperitoneal injection (at a dosage of 10 μl per g of mouse weight).
Inject 0.1 ml bupivacaine subcutaneously into the loose skin over the neck.
Confirm proper level of anesthesia in mouse by verifying lack of pain response after tail pinching.
Place anesthetized mouse on a Kopf stereotaxic frame.
Gently tighten the ear bars to support the mouse head and center it.
Adjust the height of the bite plate to ensure the mouse head is level.
Press gently on the top of the mouse head to prevent movement.
Make a 10–14 mm midline incision through the scalp.
Drill a small hole (2 mm in diameter) on the skull over the cerebellum using a hand-held needle.
Locate the cerebellum at the intersection of sagittal and lambdoid suture lines, posterior to the intersection by 5–6 mm.
Insert a syringe into the drilled hole after locating the injection site precisely.
Inject cell suspension while maintaining the syringe in place for 2 min post-injection to prevent efflux.
Remove the syringe carefully and suture the incision.
Watch the mouse carefully when placing on the stereotaxic frame.
Apply non-antibiotic ointment on mouse eyes to ensure they remain moist during anesthesia and recovery.
Make an incision (approximately 1/2”) in the midline of the scalp over the cerebellum.
Gently scrape away muscles and tendons covering the skull using a cotton swab with PBS.
Drill a small hole (2 mm in diameter) in the skull over the cerebellum using a beveled 18-gauge needle.
Remove skull pieces from the drill point by forceps.
Position the hole at 5–6 mm posterior to the intersection of sagittal and coronal suture lines.
Gently rotate the needle on the surface of the skull to make a hole without pressing strongly.
Fill a Hamilton syringe with cell suspension (5–8 μL).
Mount the syringe on a micromanipulator.
Introduce the syringe needle through the skull and into the cerebellum at a depth of 2–3 mm.
Operate the micromanipulator in lateral, probe, and vertical directions to target the cerebellum.
Insert the needle at an angle of 40°–60° relative to the mouse head.
Penetrate the syringe into the cerebellum to a depth of 4 mm.
Withdraw the needle slowly by 1–2 mm.
Inject cells slowly over approximately 2 minutes.
Leave the needle in place for 2 minutes after injection.
Remove the mouse from the stereotaxic frame.
Close the incision using a 18” PC-1 needle and Nylon 6-0 suture.
Suture the incision in a simple interrupted pattern.
Tie sutures using square knots with 4 throws.
Place the mouse on a warming pad until it starts moving.
Observe the mice until they regain normal activity levels.
Monitor the mice for signs of tumor development in the cerebellum.
